reading.body:
An entry named Accelera Data Systems in Phoenix could not be confirmed as an operating data center, and its coordinates resolve to an unrelated home-services business.

The record carries no megawatts, no operator, no website, and no business registration. A reverse geocode of the stored coordinates returns A1 Garage Door Service on West Behrend Drive in the Deer Valley area, a different occupant than the name on the row. The name itself is generic and does not describe a colocation provider or hosting business. The entry is filed as unconfirmed rather than operational.

For AI infrastructure this matters as a data-quality signal rather than a capacity one. A facility with no published power figure cannot be counted toward the state's total, and Arizona's four facilities with published figures total 512 MW. This row contributes nothing to that number and cannot be ranked against it. The address also sits roughly 15 to 20 miles from the other eight rows in its batch, so no shared building or campus connects them.

What the data does not establish is whether a data center ever operated here. A stale or imprecise map pin and a vacated tenant would both produce this record, and the research note says the search was exhausted without a confirmed operator site, registration, or press coverage. The honest reading is an unresolved name at an address, not a verified absence of infrastructure.
